Note::remove_punctuation¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::remove_punctuation() const

Delete ASCII Punctuation From Every Cell¶

remove_punctuation() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with every ASCII punctuation character deleted from each cell. Use it as a normalization step before tokenization, hashing, or comparison, when marks like ,, ., !, -, _, #, % are noise.

The characters removed are the ASCII punctuation class — the visible ASCII symbols that are not letters or digits (!"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\]^_{|}~). Everything else is **kept**: letters, digits, whitespace, and — importantly — **all non-ASCII bytes**, so accented and non-Latin text (café, 日本語`) passes through unchanged. Nothing is trimmed or collapsed, so removing a mid-string mark can leave the surrounding spaces.

remove_punctuation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Contrast remove_symbols, which also strips ASCII control bytes but likewise keeps non-ASCII.

Example 1: A Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"Hello, World! 42", "a_b-c.d", "café #99"}).remove_punctuation())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["Hello World 42", "abcd", "café 99"]

Punctuation is gone; letters, digits, spaces, and the non-ASCII é remain.

Example 2: Whitespace And Shape Are Preserved¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note({{"a, b", "c.d"}}).remove_punctuation();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 2], dim=2, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a b", "cd"]
]

"a, b" keeps its space; "c.d" becomes "cd".

See Also¶

  • Note::remove_symbols: also removes ASCII control bytes.

  • Note::keep_alnum: keep only letters and digits (drops whitespace and non-ASCII too).

  • Note::remove_all: delete a specific literal string.

  • Note::strip: remove characters at the boundaries only.
